claims.text: As-deposited non-equiatomic FeMnNiGeSi-type thin films and nanoribbons possess substrate-induced residual lattice strain.
These as-deposited films and nanoribbons have a high density of non-equilibrium defects.
Annealing at approximately 400°C for one hour in an inert atmosphere will relax lattice strain in the FeMnNiGeSi-type films.
The proposed annealing treatment will reduce the films' defect density.
Reducing residual strain and non-equilibrium defects will produce a more homogeneous magnetic-domain structure.
Strain relief and defect reduction will make magnetostructural coupling more uniform.
More uniform magnetostructural coupling will sharpen the phase transition.
Annealing will lower energy barriers and make the phase transition more reversible.
Annealing will increase the peak magnetic entropy change relative to the as-deposited baseline.
Annealing will narrow the temperature range of the magnetocaloric response relative to the as-deposited baseline.
Annealing will reduce magnetic hysteresis losses during low-field cycling.
Improved magnetic uniformity can mitigate heat-transfer-rate limitations on cycle frequency.
The as-deposited FeMnNiGeSi-type nanoscale material has a broadened and weakly defined magnetocaloric response.
The as-deposited material exhibits significant hysteresis caused by persistent strain and defect-induced magnetic-domain irregularities.
Peak magnetic entropy change and the shape or width of the entropy-change-versus-temperature curve are relevant measures of magnetocaloric performance.
Hysteretic losses can be important in evaluating magnetocaloric systems.
The proposed mechanism is specifically applicable below 1 T and at approximately 50–100 nm thickness.
Changes in film thickness, composition, or applied field may produce behavior different from the proposed mechanism.
Nanoscale surface and edge effects may introduce behavior absent from bulk samples.
